name: Ideal QAOA probabilities and observed finite-shot success
cohort: Existing 200-instance generic q-ary replication cohort from EXP-000; NOT the 64 Module-LWE instances
policies: separately trained fixed angles per qubit count
prefix_design: All smaller budgets are prefixes of each 1024-shot sequence, so budget rows are correlated.
statevector_check: Independent NumPy evolution versus Qiskit Statevector for all 400 QAOA circuits
sampling: Qiskit Aer noiseless statevector circuits with final measurements and saved memory
success: Minimum public squared-distance cost among sampled candidates equals the independently checked global CVP optimum; count all tied optima.
classical_controls: uniform sampling in the same bounded coefficient box
exhaustive evaluation of the same box
limitations: Ideal simulation only; no physical noise, connectivity cost, queue time, or hardware run.
One measured batch per circuit; exact probabilities predict repeated-batch performance on this fixed cohort.
Existing exploratory instances and trained policies, not a new independent holdout or a new optimized method.
Success refers to CVP optimality, not planted-secret recovery.
Both QAOA policies already use a search box centered on Babai.
A successful repeated-shot experiment does not establish quantum advantage.
